Therefore ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, so a circle can pass through A, B, C and D.

Figure 4 is not a rectangle, so it is not cyclic.

answers.answer: Yes, Figure 5 is a cyclic quadrilateral.
solution: DA ∥ CB and DC = AB, so Figure 5 is an isosceles trapezium and m(∠DCB) = m(∠ABC).
In triangles DCB and ABC: DC = AB, CB is common and m(∠DCB) = m(∠ABC).
So the triangles are congruent, and m(∠CDB) = m(∠CAB).
They are two drawn angles on the base CB and in one direction of it.
Therefore Figure 5 is a cyclic quadrilateral.

answers.answer: AXYM is a cyclic quadrilateral because m(∠AXM) = m(∠AYM) = 90°.
solution: X is the midpoint of AB and M is the centre, so MX ⊥ AB and m(∠AXM) = 90°.
Y is the midpoint of AC, so MY ⊥ AC and m(∠AYM) = 90°.
So m(∠AXM) = m(∠AYM) = 90°.
They are two drawn angles on the base AM and in one direction of it.
Therefore AXYM is a cyclic quadrilateral.

answers.answer: m(∠MXY) = m(∠MCY), proved below.
solution: AXYM is cyclic (First), so m(∠MXY) = m(∠MAY), as both are inscribed on the arc MY.
MA = MC (radii of circle M), so m(∠MAC) = m(∠MCA).
Y lies on AC, so m(∠MAY) = m(∠MAC) and m(∠MCA) = m(∠MCY).
So m(∠MXY) = m(∠MCY).

answers.answer: AEFD is a cyclic quadrilateral because m(∠EAF) = m(∠EDF).
solution: m(∠BAC) = m(∠BDC), since both are inscribed on the arc BC.
AE bisects ∠BAC, so m(∠EAF) = ½ m(∠BAC).
DF bisects ∠BDC, so m(∠EDF) = ½ m(∠BDC).
So m(∠EAF) = m(∠EDF).
They are two drawn angles on the base EF and in one direction of it.
Therefore AEFD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

answers.answer: EF ∥ BC, because the corresponding angles AFE and ACB are equal.
solution: AEFD is cyclic (First), so m(∠AFE) = m(∠ADE), as both are inscribed on the arc AE.
m(∠ADB) = m(∠ACB), since both are inscribed on the arc AB of circle ABCD.
So m(∠AFE) = m(∠ACB).
These are corresponding angles for lines EF and BC with transversal AC.
Therefore EF ∥ BC.
